assessments.rationale: Using recycled aluminum housing minimizes the release of microplastics and nanoplastics during manufacturing (parameter (p), Page 80), reduces manufacturing waste (parameter (r), Page 80), and lowers emissions to air, water, and soil (parameter (q), Page 80) compared to plastic injection molding. It also aligns with reducing the overall environmental footprint of manufacturing (parameter (m), Page 80) and energy consumption in production (parameter (g), Page 3, Page 33).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: This conflicts with the Use stage because aluminum increases the weight of the screwdriver, potentially reducing user ergonomics and increasing energy use during transport.

assessments.rationale: Threaded fasteners avoid the use of chemical adhesives, which eliminates hazardous waste generation (parameter (r), Page 80) and harmful emissions to air, water, or soil (parameter (q), Page 80) during the assembly process. This supports the zero-pollution ambition in production (Page 3).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: May conflict with the Design/End-of-Life stage if they increase assembly time or part count, though they generally align with repairability. However, from a pure manufacturing perspective, avoiding adhesives reduces production line emissions and hazardous waste.

assessments.rationale: Manufacturing brushed DC motors is less resource-intensive and requires less energy in production (parameter (g), Page 3, Page 33) compared to brushless motors, which rely on rare-earth magnets and complex electronic controllers that carry a much higher manufacturing environmental footprint (parameter (m), Page 80) and resource consumption.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Strongly conflicts with the Use stage, as brushless motors are far more energy-efficient (reducing energy footprint during use) and durable, meaning a brushed motor will shorten the product's useful life and increase lifetime energy consumption.

options_evaluated: Passive cooling (heat sinks and ventilation slots)
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling (heat sinks and ventilation slots)
assessments.rationale: Passive cooling relies on simple structural design, minimizing the number of components to manufacture. This reduces the use of energy and resources in production (parameter (g), Page 33), avoids the generation of plastic and electronic waste in manufacturing (parameter (r), Page 80), and prevents potential microplastic releases (parameter (p), Page 80) associated with manufacturing active cooling fans.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: May conflict with the Use stage, as passive cooling might limit the tool's continuous power output or lead to higher operating temperatures, potentially reducing the lifetime of the battery and motor.

assessments.rationale: A monobloc design simplifies the manufacturing process, significantly reducing production energy consumption (parameter (g), Page 3), minimizing assembly waste (parameter (r), Page 80), and lowering the overall manufacturing environmental footprint (parameter (m), Page 80) by streamlining production lines and reducing the number of distinct manufacturing steps.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Directly conflicts with the Repairability and End-of-Life stages, as a monobloc design makes it nearly impossible to repair or replace individual components, leading to premature disposal and increased electronic waste at the end of life.

assessments.rationale: Eliminating the battery in favor of a corded power supply drastically reduces the manufacturing environmental footprint (parameter (m), Page 80) and avoids the high energy and water consumption (parameter (g), Page 33) and hazardous waste generation (parameter (r), Page 80) associated with producing lithium-ion cells. It also prevents chemical emissions to air, water, and soil (parameter (q), Page 80) during battery manufacturing.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use stage, as it removes the 'cordless' utility of the screwdriver, severely limiting portability and user convenience.
